evidence.reason: The code has an unprotected waitpid/delete transition. If an interrupt lands after `waitpid` reaps the child but before `del active[pid]`, the `finally` loop catches `KeyboardInterrupt` and retries while the stale PID remains in `active`. The next `waitpid` on that already-reaped PID raises `ChildProcessError`, which `reap_completed` does not catch, so cleanup can escape and abandon other admitted workers. This is an ordinary correctness defect in the intended drain/ownership behavior.
